Hi — thanks for the clear list. Answers below (high level) and we can follow up with a short call if you want the audit package reviewed live.

1) Measurement window: We measure availability on a calendar-month basis aligned to UTC (00:00:00 UTC first day to 23:59:59 UTC last day). For customers who prefer billing-month alignment we can provide a secondary export but SLA attribution uses UTC calendar months.

2) Sampling & telemetry: Availability is derived from our per-route success-rate telemetry. We combine production inference traffic (real requests) and orchestrated synthetic probes but keep them logically separated during measurement. Synthetic probes are used to detect regional platform-wide regressions and to validate routing fallbacks; they are excluded from the primary availability numerator/denominator unless you opt-in to a blended metric. Default behavior: only customer request outcomes count toward your SLA.

Instrumentation details:
- Telemetry ingestion: 100% of server-side accept/reject/timeout events are logged; sampling applies only to heavy debug payloads.
- Aggregation window: 1 minute buckets, stored for 13 months.
- Clock sync: all servers sync to NTP and ingest events with monotonic and wall-clock timestamps; reconciliation uses UTC.

3) Credit calculation: Our credit formula is percentile-based with a minimum breach threshold. For availability SLOs we use the monthly availability percentage (successful customer requests / total customer requests expressed to five decimal places). Service credit steps: 
- If monthly availability >= 99.95%: no credit.
- If monthly availability < 99.95% and >= 99.0%: credit = 10% of monthly service fee * ((99.95 - availability) / 0.95).
- If monthly availability < 99.0% and >= 95.0%: credit = 25% of monthly service fee * ((99.0 - availability) / 4.0).
- If monthly availability < 95.0%: credit = 50% of monthly service fee.

Rounding: availability is computed to five decimal places, credits are rounded to the nearest dollar. Minimum credit issuance threshold is $50. Credits cap at 50% of the monthly service fee. Credits are applied as invoice credits in the following billing cycle after validation.

Attachments: short explainer and an example spreadsheet with a sample calculation. Happy to provide the raw telemetry export for a sample month under an NDA.

Thanks for the draft — good work. A few suggested edits and confirmations before we send externally:

- Telemetry: change "100% of server-side accept/reject/timeout events are logged" to "all production request outcome events are captured; debug-level payloads may be sampled for performance reasons" — keeps the claim robust.
- Synthetic probes: explicitly state probe IDs are tracked and available in the audit export so Acme can verify exclusion from the primary SLA if they choose.
- Maintenance/exception windows: add a clause that platform-wide scheduled maintenance windows > 15 minutes are excluded if we provide 72 hours prior notice; emergency maintenance that is customer-specific will be excluded only with documented coordination.
- Credit granularity: recommend we avoid fractional percent formulas in external language; present concrete table examples in the audit package and link to the spreadsheet for the formula detail.

Also flagging legal: minimum credit threshold of $50 is fine but check whether we should offer a pro-rata option for committed Reserved capacity customers.

I'll track edits in the attached PDF. Once you incorporate I'll send to legal for a quick review.
